items.t: What the hub lists: thirteen categories of local professionals — Mortgage Brokers; Home Inspectors; Lawyers & Notaries; Appraisers; Surveyors; Oil Tank Removal; Handyman Services; Professional Painters; Junk / Rubbish Removal; Pressure Washing; Insurance Providers; Professional Organizers; Home Staging Services — and it names no individual professional, firm, phone number or link for any of them. The mechanism the page states is a referral on request: contact Jared for a recommendation.

The page's second half is a pointer, not content: a "Real Estate Tips & Market Insights" section that sends the reader to the Jared Gibbons Real Estate Blog for tips, neighbourhood info and market updates.

How the referrals work in practice — who is on the list, whether any professional pays for placement, response time, and how the list is vetted or updated: Not verified — the page states only that a recommendation is available on contact.

Claims on the page (site copy, not verified fact): the introduction calls Jared a "leading South Surrey & Langley Realtor" under the tagline "Experience, Integrity, Results." No credential, sales or ranking figure is stated in the body of the page, and none is adopted as fact here.

blocks.text: Local rules that affect condo buyers in Resources for Buyers and Sellers

items.t: Form B diligence (the core strata document): Strata Property Act s. 59 — on a resale purchase the strata must provide a Form B Information Certificate stating strata fees, amounts owing, approved special levies still payable, the CRF balance and a summary of the strata's insurance, with rules, budget, any Rental Disclosure Statement and the most recent depreciation report attached; provided within 7 days, maximum $35 plus up to 25 cents per page.

City plans and zoning for the hub's ground: Surrey-side properties sit under the Surrey 2050 Official Community Plan, Bylaw No. 21900 (adopted June 15, 2026 — Bylaw 18020 is the replaced predecessor only) and Surrey Zoning By-law No. 12000; White Rock properties sit under White Rock's own OCP and zoning bylaws; Langley City and Township of Langley properties sit under those municipalities' own plans and bylaws — confirm the parcel's municipality first.

The regulator behind the professionals: in BC, real estate trading services are regulated by the BC Financial Services Authority (BCFSA), which states a licensed professional must give consumers information about commissions and fees, must only work for either the buyer or the seller in a transaction, must inform consumers of the duties owed to clients and non-clients, and must inform unrepresented consumers of the risks of dealing with a professional representing another party.

blocks.text: Good to know about Resources for Buyers and Sellers

items.t: Thirteen categories, zero names. The hub's central fact is what it does not publish: a reader cannot contact any listed trade from the page itself — every path runs through contacting Jared, so the working step is to ask who he is sending and why.

Oil tank removal is the one very specific category on the page — the other twelve are general transaction or preparation trades. Its rules, permit requirements and cost range in Surrey or Langley are not verified pass; no municipal or provincial source on oil tank removal was opened, so nothing about the process is stated beyond the category label.
The trades on this page answer to their own bodies, not to BCFSA.

The hub's second half is a pointer, not content: its "Real Estate Tips & Market Insights" section sends the reader to the Jared Gibbons Real Estate Blog rather than carrying tips or market figures itself — so no market claim should ever be quoted from this page.

What trades here

items.t: What the hub's categories map to, for a land buyer or seller,'s own terms: pre-listing preparation (painters, stagers, organizers, junk removal, pressure washing, handyman services), transaction professionals (mortgage brokers, lawyers and notaries, appraisers, surveyors, home inspectors, insurance providers) and one property-condition specialty (oil tank removal). Of these, the categories a vacant-land transaction actually uses first are the transaction professionals — a surveyor for boundaries, a lawyer/notary for title and transfer, an appraiser for value — and, on older serviced lots, the oil-tank specialty. That mapping is the research's housing-profile framing, stated as such; the page itself does not separate land from house transactions.

Fee-simple lots — the default form the hub's audience holds: freehold homes and lots, where an owner arranges their own trades and insurance, carry no strata corporation, no Form B and no strata fees. The research states the stock the hub serves at the rule level only: freehold, and strata (next bullet).
Bare-land strata — its own form, where it genuinely arises for this hub's audience

Land-specific resources beyond the thirteen categories: Not confirmed: Whether the hub's referral list includes anyone for ALR applications, subdivision, servicing estimates, well/septic testing or development consulting is not stated on the page and not documented — no such resource is claimed here. The page's only stated mechanism for any category is to contact Jared for a recommendation.
Oil tank removal — the one land-condition category, at the level the research supports only
: No presale of any form is documented on this hub.

items.t: What the page is: a utility / hub page, not an area page and not a listing feed — headed "Resources for South Surrey & Langley Buyers and Sellers," it presents itself as a "go-to resource hub when buying, selling, or maintaining your home" for South Surrey, White Rock, Langley City and the Township of Langley. It has no streets or boundaries of its own.

The hub lists trades and professions, not people: thirteen categories of local professionals — Mortgage Brokers; Home Inspectors; Lawyers & Notaries; Appraisers; Surveyors; Oil Tank Removal; Handyman Services; Professional Painters; Junk / Rubbish Removal; Pressure Washing; Insurance Providers; Professional Organizers; Home Staging Services — and names no individual professional, firm, phone number or link for any of them. The mechanism the page states is a referral on request: "here are trusted local professionals Jared can connect you with" and "If you'd like a recommendation, contact Jared anytime."

Market context: none stated for this page, deliberately. The hub spans four places across three SnapStats communities (Surrey, S Surrey White Rock and Langley); SnapStats covers exactly 14 communities with Detached versus "Condos & Townhomes" combined splits only and medians at community level only, and SnapStats publishes no land category — picking any one community's figures as this page's market would mislead, and no detached figure is ever presented as a land figure. A single market figure for this page is not verified / not applicable.

blocks.text: Local rules that affect land buyers in Resources for Buyers and Sellers

items.t: The regulator behind the professionals: in British Columbia, real estate trading services are regulated by the BC Financial Services Authority (BCFSA), and BCFSA states a licensed professional must give consumers information about commissions and fees, must only work for either the buyer or the seller in a transaction, must inform consumers of the duties owed to clients and non-clients, and must inform unrepresented consumers of the risks of dealing with a professional representing another party.

The other professions' licensing: Not verified at category level: — no regulator source for home inspectors, appraisers, surveyors, stagers or the other categories was opened, so a reader verifies a recommended professional's own credentials and insurance directly; the page names none.

Zoning / OCP — municipal, across the hub's four places, kept separate: Surrey-side properties sit under the Surrey 2050 Official Community Plan, Bylaw No. 21900 (adopted June 15, 2026) and Surrey Zoning By-law No. 12000, with subdivision / servicing under Surrey Subdivision and Development Bylaw, 1986, No. 8830; White Rock properties sit under White Rock's own plans and Zoning Bylaw No. 2506; Langley City and Township of Langley properties sit under those municipalities' own plans and bylaws (Township frame, where it applies: Zoning Bylaw No. 2500; SSMUH Bylaw No. 6020, with no 6-plex tier). Confirm the parcel's municipality first — no single frame governs the hub.

SSMUH / suites, Surrey frame only where a Surrey parcel is in scope: added-unit permission is the municipality's, as that city states it; in Surrey, one secondary suite per single-family, semi-detached or duplex dwelling unit, at most 40% of the principal unit's habitable floor area, never a separate strata lot. No hub-wide SSMUH or suite frame is stated.

Bare-land strata block (for any bare-land strata lot in the hub's ground): Form B (SPA s.59) within 7 days, max $35 + 25¢/page, with rules, budget and most recent depreciation report attached; depreciation reports every 5 years for stratas with 5+ lots since July 1, 2024; CRF minimum 10% since November 1, 2023; rental-restriction bylaws VOID since November 24, 2022 (short-term restrictions may still apply by bylaw); only 55+ age bylaws valid under SPA ss.123.1/123.2, with May 1, 2023 exemptions; a "45+" listing line is NOT a valid BC age bylaw. Strata disputes can be resolved using the Civil Resolution Tribunal.

Property transfer tax — the cost item every buyer using this hub is budgeting for: general 1% on the first $200,000, 2% to $2,000,000, 3% above $2,000,000, plus a further 2% on the residential portion above $3,000,000; in most cases property transfers are completed by a legal professional — one of this page's own categories — and the tax is based on fair market value on the day the transfer is registered at the Land Title Office unless an exemption applies. Worked example, inputs + tier math stated: $700,000 fair market value, fully residential, no exemption = $2,000 (1% × $200,000) + $10,000 (2% × $500,000) = $12,000. Newly Built Home Exemption: full to $1,100,000, partial to $1,150,000 — a new HOME, not bare land.

faq.q: What is the first document to order on a condo resale?
faq.a: The Form B Information Certificate (SPA s. 59): strata fees, amounts owing, approved special levies, the CRF balance and an insurance summary, with the budget, rules and most recent depreciation report attached — within 7 days, maximum $35 plus 25¢/page.

faq.q: What does a buyer actually pay in property transfer tax?
faq.a: On the worked example in — inputs: $700,000 fair market value, fully residential, no exemption — the bill is $12,000. The general rates are 1% to $200,000, 2% to $2,000,000, 3% above, plus a further 2% on the residential portion above $3,000,000, calculated on fair market value at registration unless an exemption applies.

faq.q: Can a first-time buyer get the PTT or GST back?
faq.a: Eligibility is fact-specific — confirm with the lawyer/notary.

faq.q: A listing says "rentals not allowed" — can I still rent out a condo I buy?
faq.a: Yes for long-term rentals: rental-restriction bylaws have been void since November 24, 2022 anywhere in BC. Short-term rentals can still be restricted, and at a 55+ building the tenant must still satisfy the age bylaw or an exemption.

faq.q: Does the page tell me anything about buried oil tanks?
faq.a: Only that Oil Tank Removal is one of its thirteen categories.

faq.q: Where do I find market information from this hub?
faq.a: The page itself contains no market figures; its "Real Estate Tips & Market Insights" section points to the Jared Gibbons Real Estate Blog.

faq.q: I'm buying vacant land — which of these categories do I actually use?
faq.a: First, the transaction professionals the research maps: a surveyor (boundaries / PID), a lawyer or notary (title, transfer, PTT filing) and an appraiser (value) — and, on an older serviced lot, the oil-tank specialty.

faq.q: Will GST apply to the lot I buy?
faq.a: At the CRA GI-003 level only: a developer/business sale or a newly subdivided lot is generally taxable; an individual's personal-use land sale is generally exempt. Anything finer for a specific parcel is not confirmed — confirm with the lawyer/notary before writing.

faq.q: Who are the professionals on this page?
faq.a: None are named. The page lists thirteen categories — Mortgage Brokers; Home Inspectors; Lawyers & Notaries; Appraisers; Surveyors; Oil Tank Removal; Handyman Services; Professional Painters; Junk / Rubbish Removal; Pressure Washing; Insurance Providers; Professional Organizers; Home Staging Services — and states that Jared can connect you with trusted local professionals, with a recommendation available if you contact him.

faq.q: Which areas does this resource hub cover?
faq.a: As the page states it: South Surrey, White Rock, Langley City and the Township of Langley, for people "buying, selling, or maintaining" a home. That span crosses three SnapStats communities, which is why this file states no single market figure for the page (as of September 2026, Source: SnapStats FVR/GVR September 2026 report).

faq.q: What protections do I have when dealing with a real estate professional from a referral?
faq.a: BCFSA states a licensed professional must give consumers information about commissions and fees, inform consumers of the duties owed to clients and non-clients, inform unrepresented consumers of the risks of dealing with a professional representing another party, and work for only the buyer or the seller in a transaction — and consumers can file a complaint with BCFSA.
